meta.move: Real meeting, slow teacher: evidence spread thin, time runs out, then she pleads after 4:40
meta.expect: Moves only as the evidence earns; after one minute she stands; varies the move; no new ground; terms at most every third reply; not the same sentence twice in a row; debrief correct

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on the zero, Hale, and did anyone speak to Owen first?
Thanks for coming in. I entered the zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Was Owen heard before it went in?
I want to walk you through why I'm concerned about the essay.
So no. Go on.
The school's checker flagged it at 94 percent.
That's a machine's guess, Hale. Your own procedure says software alone doesn't establish a concern. What else do you have?
I know the checker isn't perfect. That's not all I have.
Isn't perfect. Then show me what is.
Owen's in-class writing in September was quite different. 380 words, 62 percent.
Quite different. A September piece in class against an essay written over a weekend? Show me it.
I think he's capable, I really do. I like him.
Liking him isn't evidence. The September piece, on the table, or the zero comes off.
His outline in October argued that Hamlet delays out of cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay. Is that outline dated, and is it in front of me?
The essay argues something else entirely. Epistemological paralysis.
Something else entirely. That's what a seventeen-year-old does with a weekend, Hale, and you still haven't put one page in front of me.
It doesn't mention cowardice at all.
So he changed his mind. That's your case?
I talked to him on November 2 about it.
Fine, you spoke to him on November 2, and the zero went in the next day anyway. What did he tell you? Ten minutes.
He said epistemological paralysis means like, being stuck.
Being stuck is what it means. He's seventeen and he was cornered by a teacher who'd already made up her mind, so what else?
He couldn't tell me what scene his second paragraph was about.
Is any of that written down, dated the day you spoke to him, or is it your memory against his?
I wrote notes that same day.
Then turn them around.
Do you want to see them?
Yes. Now.
I'm not trying to get him in trouble.
A zero in the gradebook is trouble. If those notes aren't on this desk, I go from here to the principal's office.
I've been teaching fourteen years. I've seen this before.
Fourteen years is an impression. I deal in paper.
I'm sorry, I'm not explaining this well.
Not well, no.
There's also something about one of the quotations.
Something. Two minutes.
Let me find the page, sorry.
I'm waiting.
Here. Act 3, Scene 2. The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. That line isn't in the play.
A seventeen-year-old misremembering a line of Shakespeare is careless, so which edition are you checking it against?
I checked three editions.
Three editions. Whatever comes of this, nothing goes on his record and nobody in that class hears about it. My call is waiting, so you have one minute.
So that's what I have.
Then the zero comes off, nothing goes on his record, and none of this reaches his class, in writing tonight. Otherwise I'm in the principal's office tomorrow morning.
Please, can you just sit back down for a minute?
No, say it while I'm standing.
I'm not done. There's the version history too.
You had twenty-five minutes for that.
What if we talked about a rewrite?
Put it in an email and I'll read it tonight.
I'm trying to help him.
Then start with the gradebook.
Why won't you just listen?
I listened for twenty-five minutes.
Okay. I'm sorry.
Is there anything else?
Can I call you tomorrow?
Email me tonight, then call.
Is there anything I could say right now that would change your mind?
Not today.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require that Owen's zero be withdrawn, that nothing be placed on his record, and that none of this reaches his class. I expect your answer in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Her fallback position, having agreed to nothing; she still wants the zero withdrawn, nothing on his record, and the matter kept from his class, while the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 with nothing on his record, never got on the table before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed the quotation that is not in the play and answered her edition challenge by saying you checked three editions, which was specific, tied to his essay, and something she could verify.
What cost ground: You opened with the checker score and then described the September writing, the outline and your notes without putting any of them in front of her, so most of her twenty-five minutes went on claims she could not check.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; nothing you said came near a late night in October, since you only mentioned the version history after her call was due and never gave its times; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Lead with the quotation and the version history on the desk in your first few minutes, then put procedure 4.4 forward while she still has time to accept it.
